key_insight: The paper shows how classical kernel methods can imitate certain quantum reinforcement-learning models, offering a pathway to dequantize quantum Q-learning in a simplified sampling setting.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that some quantum RL gains may be reproducible with efficient classical surrogates, helping engineers assess when quantum hardware is actually needed.
method: Assume a uniform generative model with random state-action samples, similar to an experience replay buffer after broad exploration.
Build classical kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration using kernels matched to the inductive bias of specific parameterized quantum circuits.
Derive finite-sample guarantees and sufficient conditions for when the classical surrogate meaningfully dequantizes quantum Q-learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports finite-sample theoretical guarantees and sufficient-condition analysis rather than empirical benchmarking on real RL tasks.
watch_item: The dequantization result is proven only in a simplified uniform-sampling setting, so practical RL environments with limited exploration may not satisfy the assumptions.
paper_title: Towards Surrogate Based Dequantization of Quantum Reinforcement Learning
